title: Questions and Answers on the Collected Edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Master Lianchi said of the collected edition: “It has greatly benefited the Pure Land.”

inline.s: Master Lianchi said of the collected edition: “It has greatly benefited the Pure Land.”
Master Ouyi said of the collected edition: “This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara.”
Moreover, Wang Longshu’s collected edition was incorporated into the Qianlong Canon.
Recite it often and hear it often, recollect it often and practice it often,
so that body and mind may gradually enter the Land of Bliss and gradually arrive at the Land of Bliss.
Though one toils with diligence and effort for a single lifetime, it is but a moment,
and afterwards one is born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, where joy is without limit.
Good and evil, in the end, meet their retribution; and three feet above one’s head the spirits keep watch.
Question: Why compile a collected edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life?
Answer:
compiling a collected edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
is a genuine need in the course of study and practice

The Sutra of Immeasurable Life is the essential text among all the Pure Land scriptures. It sets forth in detail the causes and fruits of Amitābha Buddha’s attainment of Buddhahood, the adorned purity of the Land of Bliss in its support and surroundings, the faith, vow, practice and realization of sentient beings who are reborn there, and the joy of renunciation and yearning of Pure Land practitioners.

This is the scripture that those who practice Buddha-recitation must read and steep themselves in again and again, so that body and mind may gradually enter the Land of Bliss and gradually arrive at the Land of Bliss.

However, because this sutra has five translations whose contents are not entirely the same, and practitioners of Buddha-recitation find it hard to recite and steep themselves in all of them, the Song-dynasty layman Wang Longshu first produced a collected edition (
the Great Amitābha Sutra, abbreviated as the “Wang Collected Edition”
), which immediately spread freely throughout the world; it circulated everywhere and the monasteries honored it as a textbook,
and in the Qing dynasty it was incorporated into the Qianlong Canon.
This shows that the collected edition truly met a real need in the course of study and practice.
Master Lianchi said:
“What the Wangs gathered, compared with the five translations, is simple and clear, and it has circulated down to the present age
(it has circulated from the Song dynasty to the end of the Ming dynasty)
, and its benefit is very great.”
Again he said:
“Because the Wang edition is what is most current in the world, and people are familiar with it.”

Therefore in his Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra (Mituo Shuchao), wherever he cites the Sutra of Immeasurable Life he draws for the most part on the Wang Collected Edition, occasionally using the original translations. And Master Youxi, in his Round-Middle Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra (Mituo Yuanzhong Chao), used only the Wang Collected Edition. And Master Yinguang, in the preface he wrote for the Re-engraved Round-Middle Commentary, praised the Wang Collected Edition:
“Its wording and meaning are full and detailed, and it is circulated throughout the world.”

But the Wang Collected Edition, owing to the limits of its circumstances (Wang Longshu saw only four of the five original translations) and being a pioneering first attempt, has some problems — a blemish on the white jade. Therefore, after
praising Wang Longshu’s collected edition so warmly:
“Truly, it has greatly benefited the Pure Land!”
he also pointed out, with regret, the problems that existed. Master Lianchi said:
The layman’s compilation of the four translations
(layman Wang Longshu’s compilation drawing on the four original translations)
— the words are concise while the meaning is complete, the phrasing is smooth while the principle is evident
Truly, it has greatly benefited the Pure Land!
It is a pity that within it there are several unsettled points
(a pity that within it there are several unsuitable points)
(from the Daily Recitations of Various Sutras)
For this reason, later

eminent masters such as Peng Shaosheng, Wei Moshen and Xia Lianju all set their hearts on resolving the problems in the Wang Collected Edition (that is, the unsettled points to which Master Lianchi referred), and so compiled collected editions once again, using refined phrasing to teach and spread in a unified way the five original translations, in order to aid daily
cultivation:
to grasp the meaning of the sutra
(the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
, deepen faith and vow, and practice as the sutra teaches.
Combined teaching
] A collected edition is a way of
teaching the contents of the five original translations as a whole, rather than a stringing together of words,
still less a scripture itself, nor an alteration of a scripture

In this way there came to be four collected editions in all. Among them the Xia Collected Edition (the “Buddha-Spoken Mahāyāna Sutra of Immeasurable Life, Adorned, Pure, Equal and Awakening”) is the best. Its excellence is that, building on the three earlier collected editions, it drew on their strengths and mended their shortcomings, and made a fine amalgamation of the five original translations; moreover its wording is lucid, elegant and fluent, easy to recite and easy to remember, and it is especially well suited to the study and practice of ordinary practitioners of Buddha-recitation.

[Making a fine amalgamation of the five original translations] The reader may put himself in the position and consider: if you were a teaching master and now had to teach the contents of the five original translations as a whole, how well would you do? Then you will realize what an extraordinarily difficult thing this Collected Edition accomplished, and this too is the heartfelt dedication of those who spread the Dharma.
Question: Can the Sutra of Immeasurable Life be compiled into a collected edition? Can it be compiled by a layman?
Answer: The Sutra of Immeasurable Life can be compiled into a collected edition, and it can be compiled by a layman.
Wang Longshu’s standing rebirth
as an auspicious and extraordinary sign,
together with the very high praise given him by the patriarchs and great masters through the ages,
and
the collected edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life by Wang Longshu
(the Great Amitābha Sutra)
being incorporated into the Qianlong Canon (the Dragon Canon),
all
prove that
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
can be compiled into a collected edition, and indeed can be compiled by a layman
Regarding the very high praise given to Wang Longshu by the patriarchs and great masters through the ages, a few examples follow:
Master Ouyi collated Wang Longshu’s collected edition, the Great Amitābha Sutra, and wrote a preface for it, calling it
“This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara”
and gave it wide
circulation
. Master Ouyi said:
“In the Song
(the Song dynasty)
the layman Wang Longshu, having not seen the excellent text of the Ratnakūṭa
(he had not seen that translation, the “Assembly of Measureless Life” within the Great Jewel Heap Sutra)
, gathered together the four translations
(using the other four translations)
, discarded their weaknesses and took their strengths, and named it the Great Amitābha Sutra.
It has circulated throughout the world for over a thousand years

. The venerable Wanrong of the Shousheng Hermitage obtained an old copy on the market; compared with the Southern and Northern Canons, its wording and principle are both excellent, so he made it public for his descendant to engrave.
This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara,
one and the same through ancient and modern times.”
(from the Collected Works of Lingfeng
Postscript to the Collated and Corrected Great Amitābha Sutra)

[Dharmākara] This was the name of Amitābha Buddha when, in the stage of his causal ground, he left home and practiced the bodhisattva path. [In the causal stage] The whole course from first arousing the mind of enlightenment in the stage of an ordinary being until the full perfection of Buddhahood is called the “causal ground.” [Wheel of vows] The great vow of a bodhisattva, because his vows are firm and can shatter all the demons, obstacles and enemies, like the wheel-treasure of a wheel-turning king, is figuratively called the “wheel of vows.”
In the “Biography of Wang Longshu among the Scholars of the Academy,” Master Lianchi praised him, saying:
“Longshu urged people toward the Western Land with the greatest urgency and earnestness. Not only did he give expression to it in words, he truly practiced it as well.
When it came to the moment of his passing, the sign was supremely marvellous and extraordinary, shining through the ages.
Alas,
was he not a sage of the Pure Land, who had entered the market
chán
, the marketplace)
and let down his hand
(to guide sentient beings)
to save them?
Moreover he warmly praised Wang Longshu’s collected edition:
“Truly, it has greatly benefited the Pure Land!”
Only:
“It is a pity that within it there are several unsettled points.”
Master Lianchi said:
The layman’s compilation of the four translations
(layman Wang Longshu’s compilation drawing on the four original translations)
— the words are concise while the meaning is complete, the phrasing is smooth while the principle is evident
Truly, it has greatly benefited the Pure Land!
It is a pity that within it there are several unsettled points
(a pity that within it there are several unsuitable points)
(from the Daily Recitations of Various Sutras)
[It is a pity that within it there are several unsettled points]
Thus the task of later people
is to take
the collected edition that “greatly benefited the Pure Land”
and correct the places “within it where there were several unsettled points.”
Please note: Master Lianchi said of the collected edition:
“It has greatly benefited the Pure Land.”
Master Ouyi said of the collected edition:
This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara.
And Wang Longshu’s collected edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
was incorporated into the Qianlong Canon
(the Dragon Canon)
The National Teacher Yulin, in his essay “In Praise of Wang Longshu,” said:
“Books on rebirth in the Pure Land are indeed vast and many,
but for the single-mindedness of his practice of reciting the name and the refinement of his effort, none surpass Wang Longshu’s Pure Land essays!
In the past I read his book, and each time I laid down the scroll I sighed three times, wishing to spread it far and wide.”
Peng Shaosheng, in his “Biography of Wang Xuzhong,” said:
“Xuzhong
(that is, Wang Longshu)
used the Sutra of Immeasurable Life to extol the Western Land, whose meaning is deep and broad. Yet from the Han down to the Song
(the original translations from the Han through the Song dynasties)
the translations were obscure and impeded, rarely hitting the proper measure, so that the purport of our Buddha’s preaching was not made clear.
So he prayed to Avalokiteśvara,
and gathered the four versions and rendered them. After three years it was completed and divided into fifty-six sections.
The wording is elegant and the arrangement bright, and so it came to be widely practiced in the world.
Master Yinguang praised Wang Longshu, saying:
“In the time of the Southern Song,
an ancient virtuous one of our school, the layman Longshu,
named Rixiu and styled Xuzhong,
came again by the power of his vows, teaching the Dharma through his own person.
Though he dwelt in the world, he took no wife. Though he entered the National Academy
(though he passed the Academy’s examination for the jinshi degree)

, he did not tread the path of office. He gave full play to the essential teaching shared by Confucianism and Buddhism and instructed his disciples who possessed faith. He also wished that all his companions might be born in the Pure Land. As this book he broadly promoted — the words shallow yet classic, the principle deep yet manifest; humbly accommodating those of inferior capacity, gently guiding them step by step, giving the utmost expression to a grandmother’s loving heart, with nothing left undone.”
(from the Inscription and Preface to the Re-engraved Longshu Pure Land Essays)
As for Wang Longshu’s collected edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life (the Great Amitābha Sutra), Master Ouyi said:
“In the Song
(the Song dynasty)
the layman Wang Longshu, having not seen the excellent text of the Ratnakūṭa
(he had not seen that translation, the “Assembly of Measureless Life” within the Great Jewel Heap Sutra)
, gathered together the four translations
(using the other four translations)
, discarded their weaknesses and took their strengths, and named it the Great Amitābha Sutra.
It has circulated throughout the world for over a thousand years

. The venerable Wanrong of the Shousheng Hermitage obtained an old copy on the market; compared with the Southern and Northern Canons, its wording and principle are both excellent, so he made it public for his descendant to engrave.
This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara,
one and the same through ancient and modern times.”
from the Collected Works of Lingfeng
Postscript to the Collated and Corrected Great Amitābha Sutra)
Master Yinguang also said:
“The commentary

(the Concise Explanation with a Round-Middle Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, composed by Master Youxi of the Ming dynasty, abbreviated as the Mituo Yuanzhong Chao, which together with Master Lianchi’s Commentary (Shuchao) on the Amitābha Sutra and Master Ouyi’s Essential Explanation (Yaojie) ranks as the three great commentaries on the Amitābha Sutra)
in quoting the Great Scripture
(the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
uses the Great Amitābha Sutra.
Youxi took it because its
wording and meaning are full and detailed and it is circulated throughout the world,
and so he cited it specially.”
(from the Preface Exhorting the Recitation of the Re-engraved Mituo Luejie Yuanzhong Chao)
Therefore,
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life can be compiled into a collected edition, and it can be compiled by a layman
. As for whether the compilation is done well, that is another question — a matter of how it is to be improved.

Xia Lianju’s Collected Edition is exactly an improvement upon the three earlier collected editions: it absorbed their strengths while avoiding their errors and shortcomings, and moreover its meaning is lucid, its wording elegant and fluent, and it is easy to recite and easy to remember.
Question: Does reciting the collected edition send one straight to hell?

Answer: This is vicious slander of the Dharma! The collected edition was incorporated into the Qianlong Canon, and the author of the collected edition, Wang Longshu, passed away standing and was reborn in the highest grade of the highest class. How could it be that those who recite the collected edition should instead go to hell?

If everyone who recites the collected edition were to go to hell, would those eminent monks who incorporated the collected edition into the Qianlong Canon have to go to hell as well? Would Master Ouyi, who wrote a preface for the collected edition and called it the wheel of vows of Dharmākara, also have to go to hell? And would Wang Longshu, the author of the collected edition, be all the more deserving of hell? The facts are precisely the opposite: Wang Longshu passed away standing and was reborn in the highest grade of the highest class! Those who will go to hell are, I fear, still those who slander the Dharma and cut off the roots of goodness in others.

Those who recite the collected edition are, through their cultivation, grasping the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, deepening and firming their faith and vow, and practicing as the sutra teaches. What is wrong in that? That for so many years they have been ceaselessly attacked, slandered and defamed! Is this a disturbance from men, or a disturbance from māras? Should those who engage in such deeds not reflect: to cut off the roots of goodness in others — what kind of retribution is that?
Question and answer:
The guest enumerated five reasons for opposing the collected edition and used them to press the question. For ease of reading, they are now answered one by one in the form of comments.

1. In ancient times the translation of scriptures was treated with utmost care: translating Buddhist scriptures was in the past a very careful undertaking, and every translated text was examined and verified collectively; one could not “follow one’s own judgment in propagating the Buddhist scriptures.”

[Comment] A collected edition is not a Buddhist scripture itself but a compilation of Buddhist scriptures; therefore the question of “following one’s own judgment in propagating the Buddhist scriptures” does not arise.

[A collected edition is not a Buddhist scripture itself, but a compilation of Buddhist scriptures] A scripture as a scriptural text bears the name of its translator and is labeled a “translation”; whereas a collected edition bears the name of its compiler and is labeled a “compilation.”
The two must not be conflated. [A compilation] What is called a “compilation” is to gather and teach as a whole the contents of the five original translations, not to string words together,
still less a scripture, nor an alteration of a scripture

2. Compiling Buddhist scriptures is extremely difficult to do without error: compiling a Buddhist scripture is no easy task. Given Wang Longshu’s attainments in Buddhist learning, he still could not avoid faults; how much harder it is for others to guarantee the quality.

[Comment] Although Xia Lianju was not necessarily more accomplished than Wang Longshu, standing as he did on the shoulders of a giant, the later surpasses the earlier, and his collected edition is clearly superior to Wang’s. This shows that it is not the case that “others find it harder to guarantee the quality”; and still less should one give up eating for fear of choking.
3. Compilation leads to arbitrary alteration of the scriptures: compiling Buddhist scriptures would set a precedent for later people to alter the scriptures at will.

[Comment] A collected edition is not a Buddhist scripture itself but a compilation of Buddhist scriptures, so the problem of “arbitrarily altering the Buddhist scriptures” does not arise. A collected edition is a collected edition: it is a means of
teaching
and
spreading
the five original translations through refined phrasing, not the scripture itself. The two must be distinguished and must not be conflated.

4. The ancients did not circulate collected editions: ancient worthies such as Master Lianchi did not circulate the collected edition, so today one ought not to circulate the other collected editions either.

[Comment] To say that “the ancients did not circulate collected editions” does not accord with the facts. From the time Wang Longshu’s collected edition appeared until the end of the Ming, over several centuries, it
was continuously and widely in circulation
. Master Yinguang said of it that it
“circulated throughout the world,”
and that
“many people held and practiced it”;
Master Ouyi likewise said of it that it
“circulated throughout the world,”
and called it
the “wheel of vows of Dharmākara.”
Moreover,
Wang Longshu’s collected edition, the Great Amitābha Sutra, was even
incorporated into the Qianlong Canon!
Can one still say it was not circulated?
Master Yinguang said:
“The commentary

(the Concise Explanation with a Round-Middle Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, composed by Master Youxi of the Ming dynasty, abbreviated as the Mituo Yuanzhong Chao, which together with Master Lianchi’s Commentary (Shuchao) on the Amitābha Sutra and Master Ouyi’s Essential Explanation (Yaojie) ranks as the three great commentaries on the Amitābha Sutra)
in quoting the Great Scripture
(the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
, it is the Great Amitābha Sutra. Youxi chose it because its wording and meaning are full and detailed,
and it is circulated throughout the world,
and so he cited it specially.”
(from the Preface Exhorting the Recitation of the Re-engraved Mituo Luejie Yuanzhong Chao):
“Wang Longshu’s Great Amitābha Sutra, from the Song to the end of the Ming,
many people held and practiced.”
(from the Collected Writings of the Dharma Master Yinguang
Letter in Reply to a Certain Layman of Yongjia)
Master Ouyi said:
“In the Song
(the Song dynasty)
the layman Wang Longshu, having not seen the excellent text of the Ratnakūṭa
(he had not seen that translation, the “Assembly of Measureless Life” within the Great Jewel Heap Sutra)
, gathered together the four translations
(using the other four translations)
, discarded their weaknesses and took their strengths, and named it the Great Amitābha Sutra.
It has circulated throughout the world
, for over a thousand years.

The venerable Wanrong of the Shousheng Hermitage obtained an old copy on the market; compared with the Southern and Northern Canons, its wording and principle are both excellent, so he made it public for his descendant to engrave.
This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara,
one and the same through ancient and modern times.”
(from the Collected Works of Lingfeng
Postscript to the Collated and Corrected Great Amitābha Sutra)

5. Collected editions furnish a handle to those who attack Buddhism: compiling Buddhist scriptures gives opponents of Buddhism the pretext that “the scriptures were made up by later people and were not translated from India.”
[Comment] A collected edition is not a Buddhist scripture itself but a compilation of Buddhist scriptures, so this pretext does not exist.
Here there is a question that gives one much to ponder:

For the undertaking of compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life — a great work of spreading the Dharma and delivering beings — the eminent monks of every age have given unanimous approval, the attitude of the patriarchs of the Pure Land school is very clear, and the wide circulation of the Wang Collected Edition further confirms that compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life is a real need in the study and practice of the Pure Land school, with not a word of dissent in eight hundred years. Why is it that now some people rack their brains to distort Master Yinguang’s instructions, resorting to threats and abuse and launching personal attacks, and fanatically oppose the compilation of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life? What is their true motive? What do they really intend to achieve? And what is it that is truly going on in their minds?
Conclusion:

No sooner had Wang Longshu’s collected edition appeared than it at once swept the world. Master Ouyi personally collated and engraved Wang Longshu’s collected edition and wrote a preface in praise of it:
“It circulated throughout the world for over a thousand years … This is the wheel of vows of Dharmākara.”
Master Lianchi, even while pointing out its unsuitable points, still praised it, saying:
“Truly, it has greatly benefited the Pure Land!”

By the Qing dynasty it had even been incorporated into the Qianlong Canon! All this shows that compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life truly met a real need in the course of study and practice, and was a great undertaking for spreading the Dharma and delivering beings. The reason the Wang Collected Edition later ceased to be current is that Master Lianchi pointed out its error of “rigidly holding that the three grades are precisely the nine grades.” As for the forty-eight vows, they have been in circulation from ancient times to the present. The later Wei Collected Edition, although it correctly compiled the section on the three grades of rebirth, nevertheless had twenty-four vows. The Xia Collected Edition, while surpassing the first two collected editions and being very popular, regrettably still has twenty-four vows. Moreover the forty-eight vows as found in the Buddha-Spoken Sutra of Immeasurable Life have long been widely upheld
, so they ought to be adopted in the collected edition.

Therefore, as the task and mission of later generations, it is not to negate compilation but to stand on the shoulders of our predecessors and do the compilation better, so as to spread the fundamental sacred text of the Pure Land school, the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, and truly meet the real needs of study and practice.
Question: The Sutra of Immeasurable Life has five original translations and four collected editions; in daily study and practice which text should one recite?

Answer: This depends on each person’s particular circumstances. Whichever text helps you better grasp the meaning of the sutra and cultivate through it, recite that one. Of course, you may also take turns reciting several texts. But whichever way you adopt, the key is to:
correctly grasp the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, deepen and firm up your faith and vow, and practice as the sutra teaches.
Hold fast to this:
Though one toils with diligence and effort for a single lifetime, it is but a moment; and afterwards one is born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, where joy is without limit.
